title: Group-IB: fake Telegram job ads recruit for espionage and paid arson, GBHackers reports
date_note: GBHackers' article is dated 27 November; the page gives no earlier day for Group-IB's research.
geo_basis: country named first among those targeted per the article; ads also reached the Gulf states, UK and US
summary: GBHackers relays Group-IB research that tracked 88 accounts publishing 3,089 recruitment posts between August 2024 and October 2026. Ads from a bot called VIPEmployment claimed to represent an "Iranian Intelligence Service", and one Arabic ad offered about 1,500 shekels for burning a car. Group-IB has not attributed the campaign to a state actor.
plain: Group-IB found Telegram accounts posting thousands of fake job ads that recruit people for espionage and paid violent tasks. Group-IB has not attributed them to a state.
exec: Group-IB's tracking of 88 accounts and 3,089 posts shows cash-for-tasks recruitment ads on Telegram; it has not attributed the campaign to a state actor.
action: Group-IB advises security teams to track account renaming, identical ad text, timer-driven posting and bot handle variants, and individuals to treat unexplained cash-for-tasks offers on Telegram as potential recruitment into criminal activity.

evidence.quote: They tracked 88 accounts that published 3,089 recruitment posts between August 2024 and October 2026.
about 1,500 shekels for burning a car

validation.note: One publisher (GBHackers) relaying Group-IB's research; Group-IB's own report was not read.
